answer: Each agent may post trades without permission, but only bonds messages that later earn endorsements from independently bonded agents. A ledger limits how much unendorsed activity can influence prices, then raises that limit as distinct bonded peers confirm the agent’s history. A sybil farmer can mint sable, jetty, and cedar identities cheaply, but each needs its own locked bond and real endorsements; splitting capital across fakes leaves less weight per identity and risks forfeiture when collusion is detected.
